title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 239 (Preservation of books and papers of amalgamated companies)

content.overview: Section 239 provides that the books and papers of a company which has been amalgamated with, or whose shares have been acquired by, another company under this Chapter shall not be disposed of without the prior permission of the Central Government, and that before granting such permission the Central Government may appoint a person to examine the books and papers for the purpose of ascertaining whether they contain any evidence of the commission of an offence in connection with the promotion, formation or management of either company or in connection with the amalgamation or the acquisition of shares.
content.glance: Books and papers of amalgamated company (or company whose shares were acquired under the Chapter) must not be disposed of without prior CG permission; CG may appoint a person to examine the books before granting permission to check for evidence of offence.
content.study: The books and papers of a company which has been amalgamated with, or whose shares have been acquired by, another company under this Chapter shall not be disposed of without the prior permission of the Central Government and before granting such permission, that Government may appoint a person to examine the books and papers for the purpose of ascertaining whether they contain any evidence of the commission of an offence in connection with the promotion or formation, or the management of the affairs, of the transferor company or of the transferee company, or in connection with the amalgamation or the acquisition of the shares. Current-law framing: identify books of an amalgamated company or a company whose shares were acquired under Chapter XV; prohibit disposal without prior CG permission; note CG may appoint an examiner before granting permission. The duty survives the scheme and any dissolution of the transferor without winding up under s. 232.

sections.heading: Preservation Duty
sections.body: Books and papers of a company amalgamated with, or whose shares have been acquired by, another company under this Chapter shall not be disposed of without prior permission of the Central Government.

sections.heading: Examination Before Permission
sections.body: Before granting permission, the Central Government may appoint a person to examine the books and papers for evidence of any offence in connection with promotion, formation, management, amalgamation or acquisition of shares.

sections.heading: Who Holds the Records
sections.body: The transferee (or acquiring) company preserves the records of the amalgamated or acquired company; the section continues to apply after the scheme takes effect.

provisions.title: Preservation of books and papers of amalgamated companies

examples.title: Destruction without permission
examples.body: After amalgamation under s. 232, the transferee company destroys the transferor's statutory registers without Central Government permission. Section 239 is breached.

examples.title: Examination before permission
examples.body: The transferee applies for permission to dispose of old books of the amalgamated company. The Central Government appoints a person under s. 239 to examine whether the books contain evidence of an offence before deciding the application.

hypotheticals.question: Does dissolution of the transferor without winding up under s. 232 free the transferee from preserving its books?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 239 expressly requires that the books and papers of a company which has been amalgamated shall not be disposed of without prior Central Government permission. Dissolution without winding up does not displace that duty.

distinctions.title: Preservation of books (s. 239) vs merger/amalgamation (s. 232)
distinctions.left: Duty not to dispose of amalgamated company's books without CG permission
distinctions.right: Tribunal sanction, transfer of property, dissolution without winding up

misconceptions.trap: Once the amalgamation is complete, the transferee may freely destroy the transferor's books.
misconceptions.correction: Section 239 requires prior permission of the Central Government before disposal, and the Government may examine the books for evidence of offences first.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 239 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify amalgamated or acquired company's books. II. Confirm no disposal without CG permission. III. Note examination power. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Amalgamation facts; disposal or proposed disposal; permission status; precise relief.

examTips: No disposal without prior CG permission.
CG may examine books for offence evidence before permission.
Duty survives scheme and dissolution without winding up.
